briefs.source_chain: FOMC unanimously hikes 25bp to 3.75-4.0% with dots showing broad expectation of at least one more 2026 hike and elevated 2027/longer-run dots therefore JPMorgan flags this as hard to reconcile with Warsh's 'hard-pressed to call policy restrictive'/'dose of accommodation' framing therefore growth and inflation forecast revisions (resilient spending, upside GDP risk skew, lower unemployment forecast, higher core inflation) point to the Committee shifting focus from supply-shock inflation to demand-led overheating risk therefore JPMorgan keeps its own call for one more December hike, in line with the median dot.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: unanimous 25bp hike, hawkish dots (12/4/2 split, 14/18 on 2027, slow 2028-29 normalization), longer-run dot up to 3.25% clashing with Warsh's non-restrictive/'dose of accommodation' language, growth/inflation revisions read as a pivot toward demand-led overheating risk, JPMorgan holds its December-hike call.

distortions.what: Brief renders Warsh's quote as 'calling policy non-restrictive'; source has him 'hard-pressed to describe policy as restrictive' as a direct quote paraphrase.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both convey the same substantive claim (Warsh does not view policy as restrictive), just phrased affirmatively instead of via the source's double-negative construction.

briefs.source_chain: Fed delivers its first hike since 2023 (25bp to 3.75-4.00%, unanimous, hawkish dots) therefore markets price ~75bp more by June and ~50% October-hike odds, sending 2yr/10yr yields to multi-year highs and pressuring equities (banks/energy hit hardest) therefore DB's economists reinforce their call for 50bp more via December/March hikes therefore the equity/yield damage is partly offset by an oil pullback on easing (if inconsistently reported) Saudi pipeline/tanker news and Libyan output restoration therefore separately, in-line UK CPI cuts BoE surprise-hike odds and a strong US retail sales beat lifts Atlanta Fed GDPNow even as NAHB housing data softens.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same figures throughout (75bp by June, ~50% October odds, 2yr at 4.74%, 10yr at 5.02%, S&P -0.45% led by banks/energy, DB's 50bp December+March call, oil-driven cushion, UK BoE odds 9% from 23%, GDPNow +5.1%, NAHB 12-month low).

distortions.what: Brief states Saudi Arabia 'signaled faster pipeline repairs' as settled fact; source notes Bloomberg's faster-repair report sat alongside an earlier, unresolved Reuters report of pipeline damage and says 'reporting on the issue has not been entirely consistent.'
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — the oil-pullback-cushions-equities read holds regardless of which report is emphasized; the dropped caveat is about reporting reliability, not the price/market outcome.

distortions.what: Brief says Libya 'restored output' (completed); source says Libya 'was restoring normal oil output' (in progress).
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — tense compression only, direction of the oil-supply narrative is unchanged.

briefs.source_chain: Oil supply fears (Yanbu loading suspension, Libyan field outages, no Hormuz resolution) push Brent/WTI sharply higher and revive stagflation concern therefore that drives Treasury and European yields to multi-year highs (10yr above 5% for the first time since 2007, confirmed by real yields/30yr/a weak 20yr auction and post-2007-09 European highs even as ECB October-hike odds fall) therefore equities and Bitcoin sell off but stay within single digits of their highs therefore separately, Fed hike odds rose from ~30% in July to 94% today on Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole pivot plus a strong jobs report and hot core CPI, with DB expecting the hike and framing the key question as how hawkish the guidance/dot plot will be.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same figures throughout (Brent +2.90% to $108.75, WTI +4.38% to $105.83, 10yr above 5% first since 2007, 30yr/real-yield/20yr-auction confirmation, European post-2007/08/09 highs, S&P 6-week low, STOXX 3-month low, Bitcoin's worst day in 3 months, 30%→94% Fed-odds arc, DB expects hike with guidance as the open question).

distortions.what: Brief shortens 'a digital asset market structure bill failed to pass a procedural vote in the Senate' to 'a Senate crypto bill failed.'
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — same event, same causal link to the Bitcoin selloff, just less procedural detail.

distortions.what: Brief's 'within single digits of their highs' compresses the source's specific 3% (S&P) and 4% (STOXX) figures into one vaguer band.
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — both figures are within single digits either way; no threshold or level relevant to a trade is altered.

briefs.source_chain: ING expects a 25bp Fed hike, not the 50bp that would better fit Warsh's own critique of the Fed-guidance-to-market-pricing-to-delivery loop therefore the market prices >90% odds of a hike to 3.75-4% therefore a 50bp move could either calm the long end (active protection) or destabilize it (validating the prior 100bp yield rise and sparking a sell-off) therefore no-hike is judged unlikely because it could hurt ('kill off') the long end therefore separately, term-premium/bear-steepening pressures (rising 30Y JGB yields, thin long-tenor euro swap liquidity, persistent US deficit concerns) should keep long-end yields sticky for now, with ING turning more pessimistic on the 2027 US economic outlook.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures (>90% hike odds to 3.75-4%, 100bp prior 10yr rise, 30Y JGB/euro swap liquidity/US deficits as sticky-long-end drivers, more pessimistic 2027 view), with desk shorthand ('back end', 'kill off') faithfully rendered as 'long end'/'hurt.'
